Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@pulsehealth.com>

Subject: Renewal: Pulse Health — initial proposal and escrow option

Hi Anna / Procurement,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really appreciated the clear signal on growth expectations for Q3. Following internal pricing and capacity planning, here is a pragmatic starting point for the renewal conversation:

- Term: 12 months (July 1 2026 — June 30 2027)
- Committed spend: $360k (equivalent to an estimated 4M tokens/month)
- Upfront credit: 10% one-time credit applied at signing
- Price hold: 12 months on per-token rates
- Escrowed usage credit: 20% of overage spend (capped at $30k) to be held in escrow and applied to next quarter’s invoice if usage spikes beyond 125% of commit
- First 3 months: capacity uplift included at no additional cost (30% headroom) to smooth migration

Rationale: escrowed credits give Pulse protection for short-term usage surprises without Redwood taking an open-ended capacity risk. The upfront credit plus temporary uplift should help with your ramp.

I attached a worksheet with monthly burn scenarios (Pulse_Renewal_Initial_Offer.xlsx). If this looks directionally right, I can circulate a redline-ready term sheet and loop legal.

Open to walk through on a quick 20-min call — do any of these times work tomorrow?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: Pulse Health — initial proposal and escrow option

Thanks Naomi — and appreciated the deck. Quick responses from our side: 

- Term: We'd prefer 18 months to lock pricing across our planned product launches.
- Discount/credit: 10% upfront is a good start but procurement will push for 15% (or equivalent in longer-term protections).
- Escrow: conceptually okay, but we need escrow applied to monthly invoices (not just next quarter) and a higher cap if our beta goes viral.
- Capacity: we need guaranteed burst to 50% above commit for the first 60 days, not just 30% for 90 days.

Procurement (cc'd) will take the official redline but wanted to surface those asks before your legal drafts. If you can bridge on term length and firm burst guarantees, we can move fast.

Anna Rivera
Head of Product Ops, Pulse Health
anna@pulsehealth.com

Marissa / Rishi — quick internal: Anna pushed back on term length and burst. My read: they will sign if we can give a stronger short-term burst and a slightly larger credit but we should avoid extending price hold to 18 months without commit uplift. Proposed counter:

- Term: keep at 12 months but include option to extend to 18 months if usage stays within +-10% of projections at month 9 (automatic extension clause)
- Discount: 12% upfront credit (split: 8% at signing, 4% applied as quarterly credits)
- Escrow mechanics: hold 20% of overage credits but apply them monthly (recon each invoice) with a cap increase to $50k if we add a matched-obligation clause (they commit to a 15% minimum QoQ growth floor)
- Burst: guarantee 50% burst for first 60 days, then revert to 30% for remaining 30 days (we can absorb with short-term pool)

Questions: 1) can we programmatically apply escrow credits monthly (billing) without legal delay? 2) is the $50k cap acceptable from a risk perspective if we add the growth floor?

Thoughts?

— Naomi

[Internal only — do not forward until we have redline approved]

Subject: RE: Renewal: Pulse Health — updated offer for review

Anna / team — thanks for the quick notes and the clarity on burst needs. After internal review we can move on the following revised structure: 

- Term: 12 months with an auto-extension option to 18 months if usage at month 9 is within ±10% of forecast (client can trigger extension earlier if desired)
- Committed spend: $360k (same as initial)
- Upfront credit: 12% total (8% at signing; 4% issued as quarterly invoices credits)
- Price hold: 12 months; upon extension to 18 months, per-token rate increases by a tiered 3% starting month 13
- Escrowed monthly credits: we will escrow 20% of overage spend and apply reconciled credits to the next invoice (monthly). Cap: $50k. Escrow release is contingent on mutually agreed usage reconciliation.
- Burst: guaranteed 50% burst for first 60 days, then 30% for next 30 days; any additional sustained burst is billable as overage.

I've attached a revised worksheet and a redline-ready term summary (Pulse_Renewal_Revised_Offer.xlsx; Pulse_Renewal_Terms_Redline.docx). If this works, I'll ask legal to prepare a tracked redline and route to procurement/DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm acceptance of escrow cap and monthly application
2) Procurement sends standard PO wording or redline request
3) We issue a DocuSign for signature and apply the upfront credit at signing

Would love to hop on a 20-min call today to finalize.

Best,
